title: Delete quarantine occurs before recoverable durable intent
evidence: B::quarantine runs at 2126; first AttemptReserved WAL append is 2144. recover_quarantined at 2327 requires an existing WAL record.
trigger: Crash or budget/WAL persistence failure after quarantine rename and before successful append_wal_record.
impact: Original file has already moved, but recovery rejects the nonce for missing durable deletion intent; the documented recovery path cannot resolve that transaction.

title: Delete uses two unconstrained nonce identities
evidence: Quarantine basename uses tx_nonce; WAL entries use auth.nonce (2138); recovery constructs del_<nonce> from its WAL lookup nonce at 2347. No equality check in secure_delete_scoped.
trigger: Caller supplies distinct nonzero auth.nonce and tx_nonce and deletion requires recovery after AttemptReserved.
impact: Recovery looks up the authorized nonce successfully but probes a different quarantine filename and fails to recover the actual quarantined object.

title: Cross-instance effect budget uses stale usage history
evidence: new loads .budget_usage.bin into usage_history once (1352-1364). acquire_hybrid_resource_gate invokes refresh_nonce_state_locked (1433), which reloads only consumed nonces and effect WAL (1438-1481), never usage_history. verify_budget_allowed reads the cached usage map (1640-1662); commit_budget_usage updates only its local map and appends usage records.
trigger: Create two orchestrators on the same root before either consumes a max_effects=1 policy for the same principal/epoch; provision that policy in both and execute separate authorized effects with distinct nonces.
impact: The global flock serializes effects but each instance sees its own zero usage, so both can pass a one-effect budget. Durable history records the overrun only after effects are performed.

title: Mutation receipt recovery does not restore charged budget
evidence: secure_mutate_scoped performs backend mutation at 2273 before commit_budget_usage at 2295. reconcile_wal_entry recognizes post_hash and persists OutcomeKnown at 1922-1938 without updating usage_history or .budget_usage.bin; WalRecord lacks principal identity.
trigger: Crash after successful mutation before commit_budget_usage, then restart and reconcile the AttemptReserved mutation whose on-disk bytes match post_hash.
impact: Recovery confirms the effect while leaving the principal budget uncharged, allowing subsequent distinct-nonce effects to exceed the configured total.

title: Markdown integrity check accepts any structurally present root
evidence: Lines 210–212 return True solely for a matching 64-hex root string; no content is hashed. CLI main_dispatcher.py:668–671 converts True into success.
trigger: Supply arbitrary or modified Markdown with a Merkle Root (SHA-256) marker and any 64 lowercase hex characters in backticks.
impact: The cryptographic-integrity CLI certifies text unrelated to the recorded evidence.

title: Optional evidence digests use inconsistent Merkle leaf encodings
evidence: compute_merkle_root:51 substitutes sha256(claim) when evidence_digest is absent; verify_crystal_integrity:250–252 directly interpolates the serialized null/empty digest. types.py:120 defaults evidence_digest to None and :129 preserves it.
trigger: Compile and export a crystal containing a FalsificationVerdict with default evidence_digest=None, then verify the JSON.
impact: An unmodified compiler-produced crystal fails its own Merkle verification.

title: Reject unknown backends instead of silently selecting the remote provider
evidence: The backend lookup defaults to MOONSHOT_REMOTE; task_decomposer sends the original prompt via client.call at lines 367-368.
trigger: A caller intending local inference supplies an unrecognized backend string and a configured Moonshot key.
impact: The prompt is transmitted to a remote provider despite the intended local selection.

title: Require HTTPS for remote endpoint overrides
evidence: Endpoint factories validate only urlparse(url).hostname; _http_post_single_attempt posts the Authorization header and messages to the accepted URL (lines 244-249). The OpenRouter factory repeats the same check.
trigger: MOONSHOT_API_URL=http://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions or equivalent OpenRouter override.
impact: API credentials and prompt contents are sent without transport encryption.

title: Unresolved AWAIT spins forever outside the tick failsafe
evidence: Waiting requeues and continues at 230–232; max_ticks is checked only at 350–352.
trigger: All remaining coroutines wait on symbols that no coroutine will execute.
impact: Harness never exits or reports deadlock despite its finite failsafe claim.

title: Vorticity check asserts a hardcoded result
evidence: ExecutionResult always sets vorticity_peak: 59; main later asserts it equals 59.
trigger: Execute any source reaching return, including one that changes the vorticity computation.
impact: The assertion cannot detect incorrect vorticity and the success message overstates the arithmetic evidence.

title: Residual purge deletes active Git lock files without checking ownership
evidence: Every *.lock whose path contains .git is unlinked at 58–62, with no process, age, or lock-owner check; command-line main invokes purge_repository_residuals at 95.
trigger: Run this maintenance script while Git holds index.lock, packed-refs.lock, or another repository lock.
impact: Removes mutual exclusion for an active Git operation, permitting concurrent writers and potentially losing repository updates.

title: Residual purge treats every scratch database and WAL as disposable
evidence: scratch.glob("*.db*") unlinks all matches at 69–72; no temporary marker, age, open-database check, backup, or WAL checkpoint is required.
trigger: Run purge while a scratch SQLite database contains required data or is open with uncheckpointed writes.
impact: Deletes database and sidecar files indiscriminately, causing data loss or breaking active database users.

title: Compiler README links resolve outside the repository root targets
evidence: Links ../../../proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean and ../../../CLAIMS.toml resolve to 00_ABZU_KERNEL/proof/lean/BabylonTrace.lean and 00_ABZU_KERNEL/CLAIMS.toml, rather than root proof/lean and CLAIMS.toml; the same prefix occurs on line 7.
trigger: Reader follows proof or claims links from the compiler README.
impact: The documented evidence links do not point to the intended root proof and claims files.

title: Anomaly filter skips the configured event limit
evidence: total increments for every block; OK blocks continue at lines 88–89 before max_events is checked at lines 107–108.
trigger: Run --anomaly-only --max N against an all-OK or long healthy stream.
impact: Process keeps consuming beyond N events and can wait indefinitely for an anomaly despite the configured bound.

title: Negative compliance statuses render as successful
evidence: status_ok uses substring PASS or CUMPLIDO; both fallback line 381 and templates/compliance_matrix.html.j2:17 render this boolean as a green check.
trigger: An article status is INCUMPLIDO, NO CUMPLIDO, or NOT PASSED.
impact: A failing article is visually marked compliant in exported audit reports.

title: Reject negative token usage before cost accounting
evidence: effective_cost_units adds cached_tokens*0.05 and output_tokens*5 without validation; record_step accepts these directly at lines 79-86. Targeted consumer search found the isolated frontier assimilation tests, no production enforcement integration.
trigger: record_step(0, -100, verified_outcome=True) records -500 effective units.
impact: The public lease API can decrease consumed_units and increase remaining_units; its advertised fail-closed accounting does not hold for invalid usage values. No production budget bypass is established.

title: Media gate ignores ffmpeg measurement failure
evidence: ffmpeg runs with check=False; lines 428-442 parse stderr and evaluate metrics without checking ebur_res.returncode.
trigger: Measurement process emits an in-range loudness/peak summary but exits nonzero (for example after a decode or output failure).
impact: The gate may return verified=True and cache the artifact despite an unsuccessful measurement command.

title: Reset research state between independent cycles
evidence: Engine and memory are initialized in __init__; every verifier and synthesis iterates self.engine.statements. execute_research_cycle clears scheduler.nodes only (192), while engine.assert_hypothesis appends to statements.
trigger: Reuse one AutodidactSwarmTopology instance for a second unrelated topic.
impact: Previous-topic statements and falsifications are included in the new crystal and can satisfy the two-premise synthesis threshold, contaminating independent research results.

title: Scope the semantic-entropy correctness claim to supplied constraints
evidence: ADR claims zero false negatives and 100% neutralization of systematic false beliefs. Its referenced module explicitly says supplied SAT does not establish external factual truth (semantic_entropy.rs:25-41) and evaluate accepts caller-supplied SolverOutcome (170-180). The assigned demo passes literal true/false at 194/201/208/215 instead of invoking a solver.
trigger: A reader relies on the ADR as evidence that the implementation detects arbitrary factual falsehoods or that its benchmark measured SMT-backed detection.
impact: Documentation overstates the implemented guarantee and can cause integrations to treat a constraint classification or synthetic fixture as factual verification. No effect-dispatch bypass is alleged.

title: Mail send announces delivery after only appending a local ledger event
evidence: cmd_send only constructs CortexEvent and calls ledger.append_event before printing [SENT] Correo enviado. The ledger append implementation persists a local row; no transport invocation occurs. tests/test_optional_mail_mcp.py:93 explicitly calls BABYLON_MAIL_SENT a compatibility event with no network delivery.
trigger: Run the advertised send subcommand expecting recipient delivery.
impact: User receives a successful delivery message although the mail is only stored locally; recipient never receives it through this command.

title: Annex VI theorem claims legal guarantees absent from its model
evidence: Lines 7–11 claim impossibility of fraud/noncompliance. Lines 16–31 model only four caller-supplied Bool values; theorem lines 37–49 merely decomposes their conjunction. Lines 55–60 hard-code all four values true without checking any document, signature or log.
trigger: Use this demo/theorem as evidence for the stated legal or cryptographic compliance claim.
impact: A tautology over asserted flags is presented as a guarantee about external evidence; forged evidence with all flags asserted is outside the theorem and cannot be ruled out by it. Finding concerns proof scope and documentation, not a legal determination.

title: Unimplemented specialists are counted as successful verification
evidence: evaluate_specialist initializes passed=True (362); its catch-all branch only sets a verified message (557-559). main counts those booleans and writes telemetry/zero-failure exit verdict (640-660).
trigger: Any matrix entry without a specific evaluation branch, such as A001.
impact: Audit reports assert verification without checking the claimed invariant; missing implementations increase successful totals.

title: Audit workers approve source without reading or checking it
evidence: Worker only calls os.stat and sleeps, then emits APPROVED with exergy=21000 for nonempty files (21–32). Final verdict unconditionally says TOPOLOGÍA INTACTA / RFO=0 (78).
trigger: Run the advertised audit on any nonempty malformed or unsafe source.
impact: Output represents file existence/size as an affirmative audit verdict and fabricated quality metric.

title: JSON telemetry is preceded by an unconditional banner
evidence: Lines 121–123 print a banner unconditionally; --json only controls per-agent printing and the final json.dumps at lines 149–150.
trigger: Invoke the documented --json mode and parse stdout as JSON.
impact: A JSON consumer rejects stdout even when all underlying commands complete; the advertised M2M output contract is broken.

title: Audit result labels hardcoded assertions as verified claims
evidence: The script sets verified_claims=5, false_claims=0 and final_credibility_score from literals; it has no source loading or claim verification stage.
trigger: Run calculate_metrics and consume its epistemic_audit output as evidence.
impact: A generated JSON report presents unsupported verification and a subjective score as audit results, contrary to the project evidence contract.

title: Rust stdio interoperability test can exercise a stale binary
evidence: test_rust_babylon_skills_mcp_stdio_interop invokes cargo build only when target/debug/babylon-skills-mcp does not exist; an existing executable is launched directly without rebuilding or checking its source revision.
trigger: Run this test in a workspace with an existing binary after changing Rust server sources.
impact: The interoperability check may pass against prior compiled behavior and fail to test the current checkout. This is a verification gap; it does not establish production vulnerability.

title: Drizzle example shadows the table with the query result
evidence: const users = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.active, true)).limit(10); declares users and reads the same binding in its initializer. The snippet also lacks imports for eq and the users schema.
trigger: Copy the Drizzle example into a Worker handler and evaluate the query.
impact: JavaScript encounters the users temporal dead zone (or TypeScript rejects the declaration), preventing the documented query from executing. Use a separate result variable and import the schema and eq.

title: Benchmark prints a fixed end-to-end latency attribution it never measures
evidence: print_forensic_report always states that 70% of perceived slowness is due to the framework after successful imports. Measurements only time imports and 10,000 local formatting/template calls; there is no LLM/network or perceived-latency measurement.
trigger: Execute the benchmark in an environment where LangChain is installed, regardless of the measured ratios.
impact: The report presents an unsupported quantitative attribution as a measured conclusion; downstream comparisons may repeat it. This finding concerns generated report evidence, not actual framework performance.

title: Written confirmation is described as a substitute for hardware attestation
evidence: Step 2 permits Touch ID or confirmacion explicita imperativa; canonical .babylon60rules requires hardware attestation tied to the real hash for protected runtime transactions.
trigger: An operator/agent follows this module to release a financial mutation using textual confirmation alone.
impact: Procedure instructs a weaker authorization path than the canonical contract. This is a documentation conflict; no execution consumer or working runtime bypass was established.
